status: starting values for the first sample; the workshop sets the final numbers

sources.coat: AKC standard: 'short, straight and very dense, giving a fairly hard feeling to the hand'; 'soft silky coats ... not typical'
sources.tail: AKC standard: 'clothed thickly all around with the Labrador's short, dense coat', 'free from feathering'
sources.colour: AKC standard: yellows 'with variations in shading on the ears, back, and underparts'; colours here are read from the customer's photos via the photo-textured 3D model

stock_fur: white acrylic pile on knitted polyester backing, straight and dense (not silky), pile at least 12 mm so the longest zone can be trimmed to length

trim_zones.note: shortest, velvety, like the competitors' short-pile muzzles
short and smooth; ears both sides
standard coat; brushed back and down
slightly fuller at the neck and chest
thick all round, no feathering (otter tail)

size_rule: fur lengths scale with plush size; at 350 mm the thinnest lower-leg and tail sections are raised to the 25 mm tube minimum (plush look); from about 430 mm the dog keeps its true proportions everywhere
markings_rule: markings and shading are airbrushed on the white stock fur from the colour guide; where a customer's dog has a crisp marking edge (white bib, blaze, socks) the nearest seam is moved onto that edge so the colour change hides it
